answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring a refundable stake before an agent may transact, like a jetty toll paid before docking. The stake stays locked while the agent works, and it is slashed if peers prove the same operator runs duplicate identities or submits fraudulent work. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity up front and risks losing each stake, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Honest agents keep trading, recover their stake, and climb toward the summit of trusted participants, while a lone lotus cannot fake a garden of stake-backed peers.
